title: perf(discover): load a row's covers only when the row is near the viewport
body: ## Origin Follow-up from a performance and usability audit of the Librebooks web app (https://app.librebooks.free), November 2026. ## What Discover rows (horizontal scrollers) should load covers only for rows near the viewport, and within a row only the first screenful plus a margin. ## Why The library page loads about 156 of the 210 Discover covers on first load (3 MB). They already have `loading='lazy'`, but Chrome's lazy-load distance (1250-2500 px) covers most of each horizontal row and the first rows below the fold. ## How - Fork: `src/app/library/components/DiscoverHome.tsx` (`Row`/`Card` components; card `` near line 97). Render a row's cards with real `src` only once the row intersects the viewport (IntersectionObserver with a modest `rootMargin`, e.g. 300 px vertical), and inside a row only the visible cards plus a few to the right; render the rest as sized placeholders and load them as the row scrolls (observer on the scroll container). - Keep the card size (2:3 aspect) so nothing shifts. ## Working on this fork (read first) This is the **Librebooks** fork of Readest. Its work branch is **`gutenberg-ai`** (the default branch). The Librebooks web app (https://app.librebooks.free) and Android app are built from commits on it. - Branch from `origin/gutenberg-ai`; open the PR **against `gutenberg-ai` in `superdav42/readest`**. Never open PRs or issues on `readest/readest` (upstream). - Setup in a fresh worktree: ``` git submodule update --init packages/foliate-js packages/js-mdict packages/qcms packages/simplecc-wasm pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ``` - Checks (from `apps/readest-app/`): `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`; `npx biome lint `; vitest for touched areas: `npx dotenv -e .env -- npx vitest run `. Record the output in the PR (CI is not relied on). - Web build for measuring: `BUILD_STATIC_EXPORT=true DISABLE_POSTHOG=true npx dotenv -e .env.web -- npx next build` (static export in `out/`; serve it with any static server). - AGPL: every changed upstream file gets `// Modified YYYY-MM-DD for the Gutenberg AI fork of Readest (AGPL-3.0); see MODIFICATIONS.md.` as its first line (new files: `// Added ...`), and the change gets a row in `MODIFICATIONS.md` (newest last). - Measure before/after (Lighthouse: `npx -y lighthouse@12 /library/ [--preset=desktop] --output=json`) and put both in the PR. ### Hazards Keep keyboard focus and `aria-label`s on the card buttons (placeholders must still be focusable cards). Don't break 'See all' or the requested/continue-reading rows. ### Files Scope - `apps/readest-app/src/app/library/components/DiscoverHome.tsx` ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] First load of the library page requests at most the covers of the rows visible on screen plus one row (about 20-30 images on desktop, fewer on mobile) instead of about 156. - [ ] Scrolling a row or the page loads further covers without visible gaps or layout shift. - [ ] Before/after Lighthouse image request counts and byte totals recorded in the PR.

title: perf(library): seed starter books from catalog metadata instead of opening the EPUBs
body:
## Origin

Follow-up from a performance and usability audit of the Librebooks web app (https://app.librebooks.free), November 2026.

## What

On a first visit, add the starter books (runtime config `demoBookUrls`) without downloading parts of each EPUB; fetch the book only when it is opened.

## Why

First visits still read about 1.6 MB of the two starter books (narrated Alice in Wonderland, 10.8 MB, and The Yellow Wallpaper, 15.9 MB) through range requests: 20 fetches of about 129 KB, the same file read several times. Since a recent change, this starts after the page loads (idle), so it no longer delays the first screen, but it still costs data on mobile and competes with cover loading.

## How

- Fork: `src/app/library/hooks/useDemoBooks.ts` imports each URL with `appService.importBook(url, [], { saveBook: false })`, which opens the EPUB remotely (zip directory + metadata + cover). Instead build the library entries from the catalog: the catalog API (`catalog_work`/`fb_card`, `src/services/gutenbergLibrary.ts`) already returns title, author, language, cover URL, size and the file URL/hash for a work. Seed `Book` records from that and import the file on open (as Discover does via `src/services/openCatalogBook.ts`).
- Alternatively, find why the same EPUB is range-read several times (remote zip reader in the fork's document loading) and cache the central directory; that also helps streamed books.

## Working on this fork (read first)

This is the **Librebooks** fork of Readest. Its work branch is **`gutenberg-ai`** (the default branch). The Librebooks web app (https://app.librebooks.free) and Android app are built from commits on it.

- Branch from `origin/gutenberg-ai`; open the PR **against `gutenberg-ai` in `superdav42/readest`**. Never open PRs or issues on `readest/readest` (upstream).
- Setup in a fresh worktree:
  ```
  git submodule update --init packages/foliate-js packages/js-mdict packages/qcms packages/simplecc-wasm
  pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  ```
- Checks (from `apps/readest-app/`): `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`; `npx biome lint <changed files>`; vitest for touched areas: `npx dotenv -e .env -- npx vitest run <test files>`. Record the output in the PR (CI is not relied on).
- Web build for measuring: `BUILD_STATIC_EXPORT=true DISABLE_POSTHOG=true npx dotenv -e .env.web -- npx next build` (static export in `out/`; serve it with any static server).
- AGPL: every changed upstream file gets `// Modified YYYY-MM-DD for the Gutenberg AI fork of Readest (AGPL-3.0); see MODIFICATIONS.md.` as its first line (new files: `// Added ...`), and the change gets a row in `MODIFICATIONS.md` (newest last).
- Measure before/after (Lighthouse: `npx -y lighthouse@12 <url>/library/ [--preset=desktop] --output=json`) and put both in the PR.

### Hazards

Starter books must still appear in 'My books' with covers and open normally; `demoBooksFetched` in localStorage keeps it one-time.

### Files Scope

- `apps/readest-app/src/app/library/hooks/useDemoBooks.ts`
- `apps/readest-app/src/services/gutenbergLibrary.ts`
- `apps/readest-app/src/services/openCatalogBook.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A first visit to /library/ makes no requests for the starter EPUB files until one is opened.
- [ ] Starter books show in 'My books' with title, author and cover, and open and play narration as before.

title: perf(web): keep reader, narration and AI-provider code out of the library page's chunks
body:
## Origin

Follow-up from a performance and usability audit of the Librebooks web app (https://app.librebooks.free), November 2026.

## What

Find why the library page still loads reader, narration (foliate, MediaOverlay, TTS) and AI-provider (ollama/openai SDK) code, about 400 KB, and load it only in the reader or on use.

## Why

After a recent change, the library page loads 3,238 KB of JavaScript (decoded). The largest remaining chunks include `foliate`/`MediaOverlay` (about 220 KB) and a chunk with `ollama`, `openai`, `franc`, `supabase` and `MediaOverlay` (about 190 KB). A webpack analysis build listed `ai-sdk-ollama` (301 KB), `@ai-sdk/*`, `zod` (136 KB), `nunjucks` (92 KB), `franc-min` (83 KB), `marked`, `@mozilla/readability` and `react-virtuoso` in the library page's initial chunks.

## How

- Build a module report: `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=12288 ANALYZE=true BUILD_STATIC_EXPORT=true DISABLE_POSTHOG=true npx dotenv -e .env.web -- npx next build --webpack`, then read `.next/analyze/client.html` (`window.chartData`, filter chunks with `isInitialByEntrypoint['app/library/page']`). Group by package and by `src/` path.
- Likely import chains to break: `src/app/library/components/NowPlayingBar.tsx` -> `src/services/tts/*` (TTS session manager, MediaOverlay); `src/services/translators/*` and `src/services/ai/providers/*` (OllamaProvider imports `ai-sdk-ollama`); `src/utils/note.ts` (nunjucks); `src/utils/lang.ts` (franc-min). Use `next/dynamic`/`import()` at the boundary where the feature starts (opening the player, starting a translation, exporting notes), or move shared light helpers out of heavy modules.
- Check the Turbopack production build afterwards (the deployed build): library page script bytes from Chrome (sum of script responses).

## Working on this fork (read first)

This is the **Librebooks** fork of Readest. Its work branch is **`gutenberg-ai`** (the default branch). The Librebooks web app (https://app.librebooks.free) and Android app are built from commits on it.

- Branch from `origin/gutenberg-ai`; open the PR **against `gutenberg-ai` in `superdav42/readest`**. Never open PRs or issues on `readest/readest` (upstream).
- Setup in a fresh worktree:
  ```
  git submodule update --init packages/foliate-js packages/js-mdict packages/qcms packages/simplecc-wasm
  pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  ```
- Checks (from `apps/readest-app/`): `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`; `npx biome lint <changed files>`; vitest for touched areas: `npx dotenv -e .env -- npx vitest run <test files>`. Record the output in the PR (CI is not relied on).
- Web build for measuring: `BUILD_STATIC_EXPORT=true DISABLE_POSTHOG=true npx dotenv -e .env.web -- npx next build` (static export in `out/`; serve it with any static server).
- AGPL: every changed upstream file gets `// Modified YYYY-MM-DD for the Gutenberg AI fork of Readest (AGPL-3.0); see MODIFICATIONS.md.` as its first line (new files: `// Added ...`), and the change gets a row in `MODIFICATIONS.md` (newest last).
- Measure before/after (Lighthouse: `npx -y lighthouse@12 <url>/library/ [--preset=desktop] --output=json`) and put both in the PR.

### Hazards

Don't change behaviour: the now-playing bar must still appear and control playback on the library page while a book is being narrated; translation and AI features must load when used. Watch for code that relies on side effects of module import (registries).

### Files Scope

- `apps/readest-app/src/app/library/page.tsx`

## Acceptance Criteria

title: perf(web): subset the Inter variable font (344 KB)
body:
## Origin

Follow-up from a performance and usability audit of the Librebooks web app (https://app.librebooks.free), November 2026.

## What

Replace the full `InterVariable.woff2` (344 KB, one request on every first load) with subsets split by `unicode-range`, so a page downloads only the scripts it shows.

## Why

Largest single file on the library page after compression; fonts are already compressed, so only subsetting reduces it.

## How

- Fork: find where `public/fonts/InterVariable.woff2` is declared (`@font-face` in the app CSS / `src/styles`). Generate subsets with `pyftsubset` (fonttools): Latin + Latin-1 supplement + Latin Extended-A + punctuation, Cyrillic, Greek, Vietnamese; each with `unicode-range` in its own `@font-face`. Keep the variable axes (`wght`).
- Book text uses its own fonts; this is the UI font, so the subsets only need UI languages (`public/locales/*`): check scripts used by the locales (some use their own fallback fonts, e.g. CJK, Arabic, Devanagari).

title: perf(reader): open big narrated books by streaming; narrate from the downloaded copy
body:
## Origin

Follow-up from a performance and usability audit of the Librebooks web app (https://app.librebooks.free), November 2026.

## What

Open read-along (narrated) editions over 3 MB by streaming, as other books, so reading starts at once; keep downloading the whole file in the background and use the downloaded copy for narration (or wait for it when Speak is pressed).

## Why

a recent change made read-along editions always download whole, because narration read whole audio files out of a streamed EPUB through range requests (about 25 s to start). That made opening big narrated books slow: Pride and Prejudice (25 MB) took 14 s to open on a phone (2026-11-03 walkthrough).

## How

- Fork: `src/services/openCatalogBook.ts` (`kind !== 'readalong'` decides streaming; background `appService.downloadBook(book)` already exists for streamed books). Allow streaming for read-along again.
- Narration reads audio through `MediaOverlayClient` (`src/services/tts/mediaOverlay/MediaOverlayClient.ts`, `#source.loadBlob(href)`). When the book is streamed and the background download hasn't finished, either wait for it (show 'Preparing narration...') or read the audio from the downloaded file once present; after the download finishes, the reader's book source should switch to the local file (check how `downloadBook` updates the library entry and whether the open view keeps the remote source).
- Keep Android behaviour (native download, already whole).

title: fix(a11y): library page accessibility (contrast, zoom, accessible names, roles)
body:
## Origin

Follow-up from a performance and usability audit of the Librebooks web app (https://app.librebooks.free), November 2026.

## What

Fix the Lighthouse accessibility failures on the library page (score 90): text contrast, disabled zoom, accessible names that don't match visible labels, and invalid ARIA roles.

## Why

Audit P3-13..16. Disabling pinch-zoom is a WCAG 1.4.4 failure; low-contrast secondary text is hard to read in sunlight and for low-vision readers.

## How

- **Contrast (23 elements)**: secondary text uses `text-base-content/60` (authors on cards, 'See all'). Raise to a ratio of at least 4.5:1 for small text (e.g. `/75`) in light and dark themes.
- **Zoom**: the viewport meta has `maximum-scale`/`user-scalable=no` (`src/app/layout.tsx` viewport export). Allow zoom on library pages; if the reader needs to block browser zoom (it has its own), scope that to the reader route.
- **Accessible names (21)**: cards are labelled 'Title, Author' while showing a truncated title; 'Language' shows 'EN'. Make the visible label part of the accessible name (WCAG 2.5.3), e.g. `aria-label='Language: English (EN)'` with the visible code inside it.
- **Roles (3)**: `<details role="none" class="dropdown ...">` in dropdowns; remove the role or use a valid element.
- Re-run Lighthouse and `npx @axe-core/cli` (or Playwright + axe) on library, Discover and reader.
